## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/assess/assess_cell.py — the determination engine (rule_version: `RULE_VERSION` below).

THE STATE IS COMPUTED. Owner ruling 2026-09-09 (references/project-standards.md):
*"you have to compute it. I can't handle this load manually."* That supersedes
DR-2026-08-19 §12.5's "permanently manual" clause as it applies to `specifications`,
on contact (CLAUDE.md rule 0). Two sessions had read §12.5 as retiring this engine;
that reading is closed. What §12.5 still governs is untouched: the reasoning doc, the
Opus floor on best_practice_synthesis, the B-before-E gate — and this engine still
REFUSES data/guidebook.db outright and emits SQL for replay through
emit_data_migration.py → migrate_db.py. Computing the state is not licence to write
the canonical blob.

RE-KEYED 2026-09-09 by migration 071. The cell was (item_code × population_code) and
is now (parameter_id × lens). The item layer was emptied 2026-09-01 and the seven
hardcoded PILOT_CELLS this engine used to walk — E-08, E-12, G-03, C-02, E-06, B-10 —
were prior-version containers whose names stated their answers. They are gone with the
driver that held them; the engine now takes its cell on the command line.

RE-KEYED AGAIN 2026-09-10, AND THIS TIME AT THE POINT WHERE IT DECIDES. 071 re-keyed the
cell's IDENTITY; the engine still gathered its EVIDENCE by slug, so `parameter_id` reached
sha(), the report and validate_parameter() and never reached the evidence. `param 1 × MOB
→ stated basis=T1+CO1+T2` therefore meant "everything admitted to
accessible-circulation-geometry" — 10 sources, 8 of them flagged `tier_inconsistent` by
this engine's own report, all 10 DOWN-WEIGHTED. Two changes close it:

  B4c  gather_sources() takes a parameter_id and returns the sources holding an
       EXTRACTION for it, joined on (ref_id, parameter_id). Migration 073 made
       `source_value_extractions.parameter_id` NOT NULL and `db.py add-extraction` —
       the writer that table shipped without — creates the edge this joins on.
  B5a  a source whose tier is not derivable from its own (evidence_type, scope) is
       NON-ANCHORING and cannot reach a `stated` determination. A parameter with no
       qualifying extraction is `pending` with a gap, which is what it always was.

`--slug` survives as the topic a determination is RECORDED under. It no longer selects
evidence, and every sentence this engine emits that mentions it has been re-derived to
say so.

Implements the pure determination function of workplan/best-practices-assessment-system.md
§3 under the doctrine of governance/evidence-architecture.md, with the G1/G2/G3/G6
fixes active, tagged with `RULE_VERSION`. G2, G3 and G6 are RATIFIED
(RATIFICATION-PACKAGE-2026-07-12, owner directive 2026-07-13).

PROMOTED 2026-09-10 (register item Q4). G3 and G6 used to be implemented ONLY in
this engine's own `source_grain()`, while schemas/directness.py's
`GRAIN_FROM_EVIDENCE_TYPE` mapped `co1 -> specific` and `standard_eb -> code`
unconditionally — two implementations of one ratified rule, disagreeing, which is
a rule that attests nothing. `schemas.directness.grain_for()` is now the single
home; `source_grain()` is deleted from this module and `GRAIN_FROM_EVIDENCE_TYPE`
is unchanged, kept as the default map `grain_for()` falls back to. Equivalence
was checked by enumeration over every (evidence_type, tier, co1_source_type)
triple the live schema admits, not by reading: 0 of 336 triples differ, including
REF-00978's live (co1, 1, 'dpo_annual_survey') — the corpus's only Co-1 source,
whose co1_source_type is not in schemas.enums.Co1SourceType and which both the
old and new implementation grain SPECIFIC via the same unrecognised-value
fallback. G2's NOT_ASSESSED moved the same way, into schemas.directness, so it
is a first-class shared grade rather than an engine-local string.

Determinism: same evidence + same rule_version ⇒ same state + same derivation_sha.
Timestamps come from --stamp, not wall-clock reads, so a re-run is byte-identical and
the double-run determinism check (evidence-architecture.md §10, check 2) is meaningful.

Module roster (PILOT-MANIFEST.md §4 — no silent omissions):
  schemas.directness          grain-matching (grain_for, G3/G6 — promoted 2026-09-10),
                              scale-directness, consolidation, NOT_ASSESSED (G2 —
                              promoted 2026-09-10). Co1SourceType is consulted inside
                              grain_for() itself, not imported here directly.
  schemas.tier_derivation     tier/evidence_type/scope consistency audit per source
  schemas.evidence_state      EvidenceStateRecord / ConvergenceAssessment /
                              ProvisionalConfidenceFlag — every row validated
                              against the pydantic model BEFORE insert
  schemas.enums               EvidenceCellState / ConvergenceStatus /
                              VerificationStatus vocabularies
  schemas.evidence_source     (via enums + verification gates below)
  source_value_extractions    the JUDGMENT item (D-0168) — what gather_sources
                              now joins on. The VALUE dimension stays NOT_ASSESSED,
                              and the reason is not emptiness: no value-directness
                              grading rule exists in this repository and inventing
                              one is stop condition 4 (G2; never silently EXACT)
  v_live_lens_links           which lens codes a figure is stated in (T-018); a figure reaches
                              a cell only through the codes written there (T-019, _lens_clause)
  (lens codes are validated against their own live base tables)

G-fixes (evidence-architecture.md §4, DR-2026-07-12-evidence-architecture-unification):
  G1  T4–6-only basis ⇒ regulatory-stratum determination: design_scale='universal',
      never 'stated', code_floor_only=1 iff T6-only; T4/T5 keep GRAIN_CODE (no pilot
      source has documented T1/T2 traceability, so no re-graining is claimed).
      Engine-side (regulatory_richness(), below) — not a directness-model rule.
  G2  A directness dimension that APPLIES but has never been assessed is NOT_ASSESSED,
      not None ("not applicable"): it caps consolidation at DOWN-WEIGHTED via
      consolidate()'s existing partial-dimension path, and the source is flagged.
      schemas.directness.NOT_ASSESSED (promoted 2026-09-10; was engine-local).
  G3  Co-1 grain follows co1_source_type (dpo_position_statement → aggregate; others,
      including an unrecognised co1_source_type → specific, noted).
      schemas.directness.grain_for() (promoted 2026-09-10; was source_grain() here).
  G6  standard_eb grain follows (type × tier): T2 → aggregate; T4/T5 → code.
      schemas.directness.grain_for() (promoted 2026-09-10; was source_grain() here).
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys

REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", ".."))
sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402  -- stdlib only; the rulings several readers enforce live there

from schemas.directness import (  # noqa: E402
    GRAIN_AGGREGATE, NOT_ASSESSED, SCALE_POPULATION, SCALE_UNIVERSAL,
    SD_NON_ANCHORING,
    COND_DIRECT, COND_DOWN_WEIGHTED, COND_DISCOUNTED, COND_NON_ANCHORING,
    consolidate, grain_for, population_directness_from_match_grade, scale_directness,
)
from schemas.tier_derivation import band, check_tier_consistency, floor_mean  # noqa: E402
from schemas.enums import (  # noqa: E402
    ConvergenceStatus, EvidenceCellState, EvidenceMarker,
    VerificationStatus,
)
from schemas.evidence_state import (  # noqa: E402

def compose_value(conn, links, direction):
    """The determination's value from its HEADLINE claims; conditioned claims are branches (OR-2).

    A governing claim with an outgoing `condition_on` edge holds only under that condition
    (migration 075: "this figure only holds given a second figure"), so it is a branch beside the
    headline, never part of it (owner, OR-2: "Branches, and an empty headline when all are
    conditioned"). The edge points FROM the conditioned claim (`--from` the claim that holds only
    under the condition, `--to` the condition): an edge ARRIVING at a row conditions nothing (the
    relaxation rows point at the general claim they relax; reading them the other way would push the
    general claims out of the headline). Link roles are unchanged, so a conditioned row stays
    `governing`. Every note returned, a decline included, says how many claims are branches, and
    the notes of a headline that has branches name their denominator as UNCONDITIONED governing
    claims: a note computed over the headline alone is otherwise read as a statement about every
    governing claim. Returns what `_compose_headline` returns.

    OPEN OWNER QUESTION (OI-55 (9)): OR-2 (2026-10-29) puts a conditioned claim beside the headline
    even when it is the gentlest value; the rulings of 2026-10-30 say the gentlest value is the
    gentlest value and that the steepest code value is never highlighted. This function encodes
    OR-2 and does not reconcile the three."""
    conditioned = set(conditioned_governing(conn, links))
    headline = [l for l in links
                if not (l["role"] == "governing" and l["extraction_id"] in conditioned)]
    if conditioned and not any(l["role"] == "governing" for l in headline):
        return None, None, None, (f"piecewise only: all {len(conditioned)} governing claim(s) are "
                                  f"conditioned (condition_on); the branches are the answer"), None
    vmin, vmax, unit, note, notations = _compose_headline(
        conn, headline, direction, "unconditioned " if conditioned else "")
    if conditioned:
        note = ((note + "; ") if note else "") + (
            f"{len(conditioned)} conditioned claim(s) are branches, not the headline")
    return vmin, vmax, unit, note, notations


def _compose_headline(conn, links, direction, scope=""):
    """The determination's value, selected MOST-ACCOMMODATINGLY (owner, 2026-07-21).

    Ratified rule, `governance/evidence-architecture.md`: a determination anchors on "the
    MOST ACCOMMODATING available value, read per the parameter's accessibility direction --
    best-for-the-user, not largest-number: the widest minimum corridor, but the LOWEST
    maximum threshold height and the GENTLEST maximum ramp slope." That bullet has carried
    an `[ENGINE-LAG -> DR-2026-07-21 section 5]` marker since it was written, and this
    function is the half that removes it: every `specifications.value_min/value_max/
    value_unit` since the 057 baseline has been NULL because the engine passed literal None
    into those three slots, having no rule it could apply.

    Returns (value_min, value_max, value_unit, note, notations). `scope` ("unconditioned " when the
    caller has set conditioned claims aside) prefixes "governing claim(s)" in every note that counts
    or names them, so a denominator is named for what it counts. A NULL triple always arrives with a
    note saying WHY, because "no value" and "no rule to pick one" are different facts and a
    determination that cannot tell them apart is the pending-versus-never-read collision
    again, one column along.

    THE FOUR WAYS IT DECLINES, each reported rather than defaulted:
      * no governing claim states a number (every one is qualitative or a ratio);
      * the governing claims are in DIFFERENT UNITS that no row of `base_units` relates (units of one kind
        compose on the kind's canonical unit, exactly; units of different kinds, or a unit with no row beside
        another, have no common interval, and converting them here would invent a figure no source stated);
      * `direction` is NULL -- nobody has recorded which way is better for a disabled
        person on this parameter, so "most accommodating" has no meaning yet
        (`db.py set-parameter-direction` is the remedy, and the note says so);
      * `direction` is `contested` -- DR-2026-07-21 section 5: where the direction is
        population-contested, most-accommodating selection is INAPPLICABLE, no single value
        is anchored, and the spread is rendered with each population's direction stated.
        Anchoring one number here would silently pick a winner between two groups of
        disabled people, which is the whole thing that safeguard exists to prevent.

    SCOPE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS AN EXTENSION. The owner's wording is about jurisdictions'
    CODE FLOORS differing. This applies the same selection to any divergent governing set,
    because it is the only composition rule this project has ruled and the alternative is
    no value at all. Recorded here rather than assumed so it can be vetoed.
    """
    gov = [l for l in links if l["role"] == "governing"]
    if not gov:
        return None, None, None, None, None    # `pending` already says this

    ids = [l["extraction_id"] for l in gov]

    # source_value_extractions with only the columns its own assertions need. A fixture

    # answer rather than a crash.

            "interval can be composed from it"), None

        "SELECT extraction_id, claimed_value, claimed_unit, comparator, claim_type "
        "FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id IN (%s)"
        % ",".join("?" * len(ids)), ids).fetchall()

    # ── COMPOSE ACROSS UNITS OF ONE KIND, NEVER ACROSS KINDS (owner rulings 2026-09-17 and OR-10) ──
    # Each governing bound is placed on a COMMON SCALE. For a unit that is a row of `base_units` -- `1:12` and `5 %` are
    # two notations of one dimensionless gradient, `80 cm` and `800 mm` two units of one length -- the scale is the
    # canonical unit of its quantity kind and the conversion is exact, in Fraction. For a unit with no row the scale
    # IS the stated unit, and two different ones still refuse to compose: millimetres and degrees are different
    # kinds of quantity, and the ruling's ACTION (4) leaves that refusal alone.

    for _eid, val, unit, cmp_, ctype in rows:

            # ruling is that a RATIO is no longer in this bucket -- it is a notation
            # this engine can now read, and the 2-of-7 composition that motivated the
            # ruling was exactly these rows going unread.
            unparsed.append((val, unit))

        # named like a kind would otherwise merge with the kind's units, in an order-dependent way)

        if fam:

            f"no {scope}governing claim states a numeric value (all are qualitative, or a "
            "notation this engine does not read into a bound)"), None
    if len(scales) > 1:
        return None, None, None, (
            "%sgoverning claims are stated in different units (%s); composing an interval "
            "would require a conversion no source stated"
            % (scope, ", ".join(sorted({repr(u) for _b, u in bounds})))), None
    family = unit_kind(conn, bounds[0][1])             # one scale, so every bound's unit is of this kind or none is
    unit = (canonical_unit(conn, family) if family
            else (next(iter({u for _b, u in bounds})) or None))

    if direction is None:

            "no accessibility_direction recorded for this parameter, so the "
            "most-accommodating rule (owner 2026-07-21) has nothing to read: record it "

            "spread is rendered with each population's direction stated"), None

                  f"claims: {len(unparsed)} state no parsable numeric bound ({_shown}) and "
                  f"contribute to the cell's STATE but not to this interval")

            hi = from_canonical(conn, vmax, member, _hi_kind, _hi_from)

    """Only a VERIFIED source earns a band ("must be verified", owner 2026-10-21). An unverified

    `has_unverified_sources`, but it is left out of the marker, so it can neither raise nor lower
    it; a cell with no verified governing source is weak (evidence-methodology 2.8: unverified
    sources are flagged and do not downgrade a cell the verified ones carry)."""
    return (rec["verification_status"] or "") in VERIFIED_OK


def _confirmed_bands(conn, parameter_id, links, confirmer_anchors, lens):
    """R39: each governing source's band under confirmation by study. One confirmed clause does
    not confirm the code (owner 2026-10-21): an unconfirmed row is weak, and a source takes the
    floor of the mean of its rows, so it reaches the confirming band only when every row does.

    A row is confirmed by a `confirms` edge, whose referent is that row, from a VERIFIED
    anchoring source (`confirmer_anchors`, from `gather_confirmers`: not the direction set, which
    leaves out an `absent` row) through a finding row of THIS parameter that is
    not skimmed (`_publishable_clause`). An `absent` row confirms, because the edge is itself the
    claim: a study that tested the existing value and found no case to change it supports that
    value (owner, 2026-10-21, REF-00980: "the absence of the findings is actually research support
    for that tested code value"). The edge needs a row referent and a quote, so an absence that
    examined nothing carries no such edge and confirms nothing. A confirmed row takes the floor of
    the mean of its confirmers' bands, a source the floor of the mean of its rows'. A `to_label`
    referent names no row and confirms nothing. The confirming row is stated in the cell's lens
    (`_lens_clause`, as in `gather_confirmers`): a finding tagged for another group confirms nothing
    here, though its source is a confirmer through a row that is."""
    rows = {l["extraction_id"]: l["ref_id"] for l in links if l["role"] == "governing"}
    if not rows or not _table_exists(conn, "extraction_relations"):
        return {}
    confirmer_bands = {r["ref_id"]: band(r["tier"], r["evidence_type"])
                       for r in confirmer_anchors if _verified(r)}
    skim, skim_params = _publishable_clause(conn, "e")
    lens_sql, lens_vals = _lens_clause(conn, lens, "e")
    confirmers = {}
    for to_id, from_ref in conn.execute(
            "SELECT r.to_extraction_id, e.ref_id FROM extraction_relations r "
            "JOIN source_value_extractions e ON e.extraction_id = r.from_extraction_id "
            "WHERE r.relation = 'confirms' AND e.parameter_id = ? "
            "AND e.figure_role IN (%s) %s %s AND r.to_extraction_id IN (%s)"
            % (",".join("?" * len(DIRECTION_SUPPLYING_ROLES)), skim, lens_sql, ",".join("?" * len(rows))),
            (parameter_id, *DIRECTION_SUPPLYING_ROLES, *skim_params, *lens_vals, *rows)):
        if from_ref in confirmer_bands:
            confirmers.setdefault(to_id, {})[from_ref] = confirmer_bands[from_ref]
    by_source = {}
    for eid, ref in rows.items():
        by_source.setdefault(ref, []).append(
            floor_mean(confirmers[eid].values()) if eid in confirmers else EvidenceMarker.WEAK)
    return {ref: floor_mean(bands) for ref, bands in by_source.items()}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/tests/test_assess_cell_pilot.py — unit tests for the pilot determination
engine's doctrinal branches that have NO real cell in the corpus (adversarial
finding 2 established that PILOT-MANIFEST.md previously claimed these tests
existed when they did not; this file makes the claim true).

Branches covered here, each against a synthetic in-memory DB:
  - pure Co-2-only basis  -> stated, tier_basis CO2 (§2.2 condition 3)
  - pure T6-only, >=3 distinct jurisdictions -> provisional + code_floor_only
    + regulatory_stratum_only + design_scale universal (G1)
  - pure T6-only, single jurisdiction -> pending (fails §2.3 jurisdiction
    distinctness, per the pilot-2 richness fix)
  - all sources disqualified -> pending + all_sources_disqualified flag (§2.8)
  - UNVERIFIED present -> has_unverified_sources flag set (§2.8; D-0157 vocabulary)
  - not_applicable requires rationale; divergent requires synthesis_approach
    (schemas.evidence_state model enforcement — the validator's counterparts of
    the two mutation cases the manifest previously claimed without artifacts)

Run: python3 scripts/tests/test_assess_cell_pilot.py   (exit 1 on any failure)
"""
import os
import sqlite3
import sys

REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", ".."))
sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "scripts", "assess"))

from assess_cell import (  # noqa: E402
    NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS, RULE_VERSION, STORED_ANSWER, Refusal, derivation_handshake, determine, gap_account, population_match,
    scan_command, stale_determinations, validate_lens)
from schemas.enums import EvidenceMarker  # noqa: E402
from schemas.evidence_state import ConvergenceAssessment, EvidenceStateRecord  # noqa: E402

# The glyphs come from the enum, never typed: the row's CHECK holds the same vocabulary.
FULL, PARTIAL, WEAK = EvidenceMarker.FULL.value, EvidenceMarker.PARTIAL.value, EvidenceMarker.WEAK.value


# The scope each evidence_type needs for its stored tier to be DERIVABLE
# (schemas/tier_derivation.TIER_MAP). Derived from that map at import, never
# restated: a copy would drift the first time the ratified ladder changes.
#
# WHY THE FIXTURE NOW HAS TO CARRY SCOPE AT ALL. It did not before 2026-09-10,
# because the engine merely REPORTED tier inconsistency and anchored anyway. B5a
# makes a source whose tier is not derivable from its own (evidence_type, scope)
# NON-ANCHORING, so a fixture with scope=None would put every one of these tests
# into `pending` and prove nothing about the branch it is named for. Supplying the
# scope is not weakening the test — it is the test finally stating the precondition
# the doctrine always had.
def _default_scope(evidence_type, tier):
    from schemas.tier_derivation import TIER_MAP
    for (et, sc), tt in TIER_MAP.items():
        if et == evidence_type and tt == tier:
            return sc
    return None


def synth_db(sources, parameter_id=1, extractions_per_source=1,
             icf_links=(), gates=(), direction=None, row_lens=({"identity_code": "MOB"},), family=(), icf_family=()):
    """Minimal in-memory schema for determine(): evidence_sources +
    source_value_extractions + evidence_population_match.

    RE-KEYED 2026-09-10 with B4c. `determine()` no longer gathers by slug, so
    `source_slug_links` is no longer what puts a source in front of the engine —
    an EXTRACTION FOR THE PARAMETER is. The junction is still created because the
    fixture should look like the real schema, and a fixture that is laxer than the
    database it stands for is how an engine passes its tests and fails on replay.

    `extractions_per_source` exercises the ruled 1:N fan-out (D-0168): N extraction
    rows for one source must still be ONE source in the governing set. Without the
    DISTINCT in gather_sources, a code document's clauses would corroborate
    themselves.

    A source may carry `extraction_method` (the column exists only when some source does, as it
    does not in the oldest fixtures) and `superseded_by_ref_id`.

    LENS (T-019). The engine reads a figure's lens only from `v_live_lens_links` (T-018), so the
    fixture holds the retired lens columns of `source_value_extractions` no longer and writes one
    link row per entry of the source's `lenses` key, defaulting to `row_lens` (most cases are
    stated in `MOB`). Each entry is a dict of the link's three code columns.
    """
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.executescript("""
      CREATE TABLE evidence_sources (
        ref_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, tier INT, evidence_type TEXT, co1_source_type TEXT,
        verification_status TEXT, scope TEXT, jurisdiction TEXT, superseded_by_ref_id TEXT);
      CREATE TABLE source_slug_links (ref_id TEXT, slug TEXT);
      CREATE TABLE source_value_extractions (
        extraction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        ref_id TEXT, slug TEXT, parameter_id INTEGER,
        claim_type TEXT, claimed_value TEXT, claimed_unit TEXT,
        figure_role TEXT, comparator TEXT);
      -- T-019: the figure's lens lives in the link table (T-018) and is read through the live view,
      -- the only columns of it the engine reads.
      CREATE TABLE extraction_lens_links (
        link_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, extraction_id INT, identity_code TEXT,
        icf_code TEXT, needs_code TEXT, retired_at TEXT);
      CREATE VIEW v_live_lens_links AS
        SELECT link_id, extraction_id, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code
          FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
      CREATE TABLE evidence_population_match (
        match_id TEXT, ref_id TEXT, match_grade TEXT, target_population TEXT);
      -- 080. CREATED UNCONDITIONALLY, EVEN EMPTY, for the reason this docstring
      -- already gives about source_slug_links: a fixture laxer than the database it
      -- stands for is how an engine passes its tests and fails on replay. An empty
      -- identity_icf_map is also the honest default -- it is what a cell whose
      -- identity lens has no promoted functional mapping actually looks like.
      CREATE TABLE identity_icf_map (
        retired_at TEXT,
        link_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, identity_code TEXT, icf_code TEXT,
        mechanism TEXT, mapping_confidence TEXT, provenance TEXT, notes TEXT,
        created_at TEXT, created_by_session TEXT);
      -- 086. Created here for the same reason as source_slug_links and
      -- identity_icf_map: `compose_value` reads accessibility_direction out of
      -- this table, and a fixture without it can only ever exercise the branch that
      -- declines for want of a direction. Left EMPTY unless a case passes one, so the
      -- no-direction branch stays testable too.
      CREATE TABLE base_parameters (
        parameter_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, term_id TEXT, status TEXT,
        accessibility_direction TEXT, direction_rationale TEXT);
      CREATE TABLE base_taxonomy_identity (identity_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        parent_code TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code));
      CREATE TABLE base_icf (icf_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, parent_code TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code));
      CREATE TABLE determination_gates (
        gate_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, parameter_id INTEGER,
        identity_code TEXT, icf_code TEXT, needs_code TEXT,
        verdict TEXT, trigger_ref_id TEXT, trigger_tier INT,
        trigger_evidence_type TEXT, detail TEXT, raised_at TEXT, raised_by_session TEXT,

def main():

    d = determine(synth_db([{"tier": 2, "evidence_type": "co2"},

    expect("PROXY: two finding axes => pending_assessment, never single_axis",

           d["rests_on_proxy_inference"] == 0 and d["regulatory_stratum_only"] == 1,
           f"proxy={d['rests_on_proxy_inference']} rso={d['regulatory_stratum_only']}")
    expect("NO-PROXY: tier_basis keeps the rso marker",

    expect("NO-THRESHOLD: findings alone do not reach a determination",

           f"{d['state']} proxy={d['rests_on_proxy_inference']}")
    expect("NO-THRESHOLD: the finding sources are counted, so the gap can name the "
           "right absence instead of claiming supersession",
           d["n_finding_sources"] == 1 and d["n_sources"] == 0,
           f"findings={d['n_finding_sources']} value-suppliers={d['n_sources']}")

    # ── The marker (migration 116; RULINGS R7, R39) ───────────────────────────
    d = determine(synth_db([{"tier": 2, "evidence_type": "co2"}]), 1,
                  {"identity_code": "MOB"}, "syn-slug", "marker-anchored")
    expect("MARKER: an anchored (stated) cell takes the anchors' band", d["marker"] == FULL, str(d["marker"]))
    d = determine(synth_db([{"tier": 3, "evidence_type": "clinical", "scope": "lower_control"}]), 1,
                  {"identity_code": "MOB"}, "syn-slug", "marker-t3-clinical")
    expect("MARKER: T3-clinical alone is provisional and still full (band = evidence, state = status)",
           d["state"] == "provisional" and d["marker"] == FULL, f"{d['state']} {d['marker']}")
    d = determine(synth_db([{"tier": 6, "evidence_type": "code", "jurisdiction": j}

    expect("MARKER: a regulatory-stratum-only floor claim is weak", d["marker"] == WEAK, str(d["marker"]))

    d = determine(synth_db(_t6 + [dict(_find[0], extraction_method=_SKIM, superseded_by_ref_id="REF-NEW")]),

    d = determine(synth_db([{"tier": 2, "evidence_type": "co2", "extraction_method": _SKIM}]),
                  1, {"identity_code": "MOB"}, "syn-slug", "gap-skimmed-claim")
    cause, _r = gap_account(d)

def stale_determinations(conn):
    """The live determinations this engine wrote (`RULE_VERSION`) whose stored answer is no longer
    the one `determine` gives, as (specification_id, [the fields that differ]).

    THE STORED MARKER IS A CACHE. It is read off the sources' verification and tier, the rows'
    grading and comparators, and the `confirms` edges, and `derivation_sha` hashes none of them
    (K01 verifies only the stored junction, each figure's in-lens state read off the live lens links,
    and the conditioned governing claims, K02 only that the junction is complete). A lens link added
    to or retired from a figure moves that in-lens state, so it moves the sha and is reported here as
    `derivation_sha` (or as the lens, when no figure is stated in the cell's lens any more). The stored VALUE and its note are read off the `condition_on` edges
    from governing rows (`compose_value`): those edges are in the sha payload, so a filed or
    removed one makes the sha, and with it this check, differ. `db.py` refuses the
    routes it knows (a regrading, an edge, a source's engine-read columns); a data migration, the
    verification cron or a route not yet thought of does not pass through it. This is what
    notices, whichever route moved the input. The remedy is the one the refusals name: retire the
    specification, re-determine."""
    cols = ("specification_id", "parameter_id", *LENS_ORDER, *STORED_ANSWER)
    out = []
    for sid, pid, *rest in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT {', '.join(cols)} FROM specifications WHERE retired_at IS NULL "
            f"AND rule_version = ? ORDER BY specification_id", (RULE_VERSION,)).fetchall():
        lens = dict(zip(LENS_ORDER, rest))
        try:
            det = determine(conn, pid, lens, "", "recomputed")
        except Refusal:
            # The figures behind a stored cell can leave its lens when a link is retired.
            out.append((sid, ["lens (no figure is stated in it now)"]))
            continue
        diff = [f for f, was in zip(STORED_ANSWER, rest[len(LENS_ORDER):]) if det[f] != was]
        if diff:
            out.append((sid, diff))
    return out

"""
scripts/migrate_db.py — Run pending migrations against guidebook.db.

Spec: architecture/sqlite-data-layer.md §7 (schema) + governance/concurrent-write-architecture-proposal-2026-05-11.md (data).

Handles BOTH migration types:

1. Schema migrations: `scripts/migrations/NNN_*.sql` (numeric prefix).
   Tracked via PRAGMA user_version. Forward-only.

2. Data migrations: `scripts/migrations/data_{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}_{session-slug}.sql`.
   Tracked via the `data_migrations` table (added by schema migration 007).
   Forward-only, append-only. Two sessions can produce data migrations with
   distinct timestamps and both land cleanly on `main` — git merges them as
   text. The DB is then rebuilt deterministically by running the runner.

Order of application:
  - All pending schema migrations (in numeric order)
  - All pending data migrations (in timestamp order)

Usage:
    python3 scripts/migrate_db.py                 # apply pending migrations
    python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --dry-run       # preview only
    python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --schema-only   # skip data migrations
    python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild       # apply ALL migrations to a fresh DB

The --rebuild option recreates the DB from scratch by applying every migration
in order. Used by CI to verify the committed `data/guidebook.db` matches what
the migration history says it should be (catches direct DB writes that bypass
the migration discipline).

    pass as NOTHING-IN-SCOPE rather than a failure, and an empty scope is often simply
    true — D04/D05 examine DOI-less sources and every live source has a DOI. Failing on

    sym = "✓" if passed else "✗"
    if subject is None:

    elif subject == 0:
        scope = "  [examined 0 — NOTHING IN SCOPE]"
    else:

    print(f"  [{sym}] {tid}: {name}{scope}")

def run_checks(db_path):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")

    def subj(sql, params=()):
        """Count the rows a check is about — its subject. One scalar, no side effects.

        Named `subj`, not `n`: several checks below already bind `n` to their own
        violation count, and shadowing it would have silently broken them.
        """
        return conn.execute(sql, params).fetchone()[0]

    # ── A: Foreign key referential integrity ─────────────────────────────────
    print("\n[A] Foreign key referential integrity")

    record("A01", "source_slug_links → evidence_sources",
        conn.execute("""SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_slug_links l
            WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources e WHERE e.ref_id=l.ref_id)
        """).fetchone()[0] == 0,
        subject=subj("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_slug_links"))

    record("A05", "evidence_population_match → evidence_sources",
        conn.execute("""SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_population_match m
            WHERE ref_id IS NOT NULL
            AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources e WHERE e.ref_id=m.ref_id)
        """).fetchone()[0] == 0,
        subject=subj("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_population_match WHERE ref_id IS NOT NULL"))

    # The one populated column that holds population codes and carries no foreign key
    # (validate_population discovered columns by name and never saw it; it was deleted in step 1.6).

    """T117-11: C10 on a temporary copy of the live database, one seeded live cell per case. The

    ignore_check_constraints so its red state is C10's verdict, not the marker CHECK's."""

    verified = [r[0] for r in rows if r[2] == "VERIFIED"]

               f"verified={verified[:1]} retrieved_unverified={retrieved_unv[:1]} unretrieved={unretrieved_noroute[:1]}")
        return

    def c10(refs, marker, seed=None):
        tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        path = os.path.join(tmp, "c10.db")
        shutil.copy(src, path)
        c = sqlite3.connect(path)
        c.execute("PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints = ON")
        sid = c.execute("INSERT INTO specifications (parameter_id, identity_code, state, design_scale, marker, "
                        "regulatory_stratum_only, rule_version) VALUES (?, 'MOB', 'provisional', 'population', ?, 0, "
                        "'t117-11')", (pid, marker)).lastrowid
        c.executemany("INSERT INTO specification_source_links (specification_id, ref_id) VALUES (?, ?)",
                      [(sid, r) for r in refs])
        if seed:
            seed(c)
        c.commit()
        c.close()
        tdi.results.clear()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            tdi.run_checks(path)
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        r = [x for x in tdi.results if x["id"] == "C10"]
        return (r[0]["passed"], r[0]["subject"]) if r else (None, None)

    ok, n = c10([verified[0], retrieved_unv[0]], WEAK)
    expect("T117-11(a): a retrieved-UNVERIFIED governing source beside a VERIFIED one under ○ passes C10 "
           "(red: C10 refuses every non-VERIFIED source)", ok is True and n and n >= 1, f"passed={ok} subject={n}")
    ok, n = c10([verified[0], unretrieved_noroute[0]], WEAK)
    expect("T117-11(b): guard, an unretrieved source with no standard_number fails C10", ok is False,
           f"passed={ok} subject={n}")
    ok, n = c10([retrieved_unv[0]], WEAK)
    expect("T117-11(c): guard, every governing source non-VERIFIED under a circle fails C10", ok is False,
           f"passed={ok} subject={n}")
    ref_d = unretrieved_noroute[0]

    def _route(c):
        c.execute("UPDATE evidence_sources SET standard_number = 'T117-11' WHERE ref_id = ?", (ref_d,))
        c.execute("UPDATE source_value_extractions SET loc_clause = COALESCE(loc_clause, '1') "
                  "WHERE ref_id = ? AND parameter_id = ?", (ref_d, pid))
    ok, n = c10([ref_d], "\\u26a0", seed=_route)
    expect("T117-11(d): an unretrieved source with a route, sole governing, under ⚠ passes C10 "
           "(red: C10 refuses every non-VERIFIED source)", ok is True, f"passed={ok} subject={n}")

- Everything is green on HEAD (282 cases).
- The pre-existing C10 subject was 0 and is still 0: `PASSED HAVING EXAMINED NOTHING`, C10 included.
- T117-11's seeding is honest as a unit test of C10:
  - each case seeds a live cell on a copy;
  - `role` defaults to `governing` (`PRAGMA table_info(specification_source_links)`);
  - (b) and (c) failing proves the sources are seen.
  - It cannot prove that the engine and C10 agree (see F4).

**Live cells** (`python3 $S/probe.py <wt> <db>`, 20 cells, every active parameter × each lens code on a live figure):
- 3×MOB: provisional 5 % ○ before → refused at HEAD. The refusal names OD-99, OD-100 and OD-92, as the ledger predicts.
- 12×MOB: ≤ 6000 mm ○ before and after.
- No other value, state or marker changed.
- `design_scale` changed on eight pending cells: five MOB cells (4, 5, 6, 9, 11) moved from universal to population; 3×d450, 3×A-EFFORT and 12×A-EFFORT moved from population to universal. This matches OD-48 (a), "whom it is for" (no identity; adjudication-3 §4).

**Reserved questions.** Nothing decides OD-92, OD-95, OD-99 Q1/Q2, OD-100 or Q3 for a shown value:
- no PROXY branch;
- no log read (`grep -n -i 'retrieval_log\|manifest' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`);
- `derivation_sha`'s payload is unchanged and the label is bumped.

**OR-22b** (ledger 6183-6184, ANSWERED) says "The study's own band; migration 116's regulation-only rule (○) does not apply to it". OR-22 (4757) adds "not a regulation-only floor". So the changed R39 assertion (rso 0, ●) is warranted for its fixture, a floor claim confirmed by absence. T019-20's fixture change still kills its guard's mutation: with the lens clause removed from `_confirmed_bands`, it goes red on both trees (`$S/mut_f1.py`).

**The T-056 item 3a edit** is warranted by OD-48 (a). "The G1 line" alone would leave an ICF-keyed anchored cell reading `population`, a group it does not name.

## Findings

- **F1. The rso flip fires on a partial confirmation.**
  - Three VERIFIED T6 codes, one row confirmed by a T1 absence finding, no value shown, give `provisional ○ rso 0 T6-only(confirmed_by_study)` (`python3 $S/edge2.py` in wt-head).
  - The cause is the condition `any(confirmed[g] != bands[g])`. OR-22b covers a confirmed floor, and R39 says "one confirmed clause does not confirm the code".
  - Since T-056 item 3a, `regulatory_stratum_only` is the only home of "rests on codes". A cell that rests on codes would lose that flag, and `validate_evidence_state` line 282's "never stated" guard would lose it too.
  - No live cell is affected today: the live `confirms` edges join no parameter.
- **F2. T019-13 now skips refused cells.** It examines 16 of 17 pairs and drops 3×MOB, the only cell with a value (`grep T019-13 $S/head-test_assess_cell_pilot.txt`). The implementer's report does not list this edit. The links are computed before the refusal, so they could still be checked.
- **F3. Prose callers missing from the T-120 list.**
  - `governance/evidence-architecture.md:21` ("anchor at weak (○)").
  - `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:403` and `:442`. Line 403 says to file a code-only cell that is not ○ as "an engine defect".
  - `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/IDEAL-GRAPH.md:411` (the old CHECK; in T-117 §5's caller scope).
  - Command: `git grep -n -E '(weak band|at ○|reads ○|never ●)' -- skills governance workplan/pipeline-state-graph`.
- **F4. Case A: the engine writes a cell its own gate fails.**
  - One UNVERIFIED T4 with no direction gives `provisional ○` with every governing source unverified (`python3 $S/edge.py`, case A), and C10 (ii) fails exactly that cell.
  - This is the status quo, kept by resolution decision 6. It does pick a circle for a wholly unverified basis, OD-99 Q1's ground, even though Q1 is literally worded for a shown value.
- **F5. The OD-92 refusal fires on any interval whose two bounds come from different sources** (case E). Its text, "several sources state the shown value", is inaccurate there.
- **F6. A cell keyed on `ALL` is written as `population`** (case I). OD-31 and OD-48 read `ALL` as universal. This is pre-existing, the T-056 items 1 to 3 residue.
- **F7. `band(3|4, grey)` stays ○.** It is "never displayed" only while grey never governs. If OD-97 (a) is answered, a no-value grey cell would show ○ through `floor_mean`, against OD-64. T4 grey has moved from ◐ to ○, with no live rows (`select tier, evidence_type, count(*) from evidence_sources where evidence_type='grey' group by 1,2`).
- **F8. T-117 §9 still says to stop if a value or state changes.** 3×MOB's state did change, as OD-92 and OD-99 Meanwhile require, but `d13caa4d` did not amend §9.
- **F9. C10, a blocking gate, now reads the retrieval log** through a cwd patch. With no manifest on disk, every non-VERIFIED T1 to T3 source fails. The subject is 0 today.
